question.text: Under SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations 2003, 'fraud' in connection with securities includes which of the following?

answer.text: Only wilful misstatement that causes financial loss to the counterparty
Only insider trading under a separate insider-trading regulation
Only acts by registered intermediaries, not by issuers themselves
Any act, expression, omission or concealment to induce another person to deal in securities — with or without wrongful gain or loss

explanation.text: The Logic: Reg 2(1)(c) of PFUTP 2003 defines fraud inclusively — any act, expression, omission or concealment committed to induce another person (or his agent) to deal in securities. The Regulation expressly says that wrongful gain OR loss is NOT a necessary element. Thus reckless misrepresentations, concealment of material fact, or promises made without intent to perform are all in scope. The Trap: A is too narrow (requires loss). C confuses PFUTP with the separate PIT Regulations 2015. D is wrong — PFUTP applies to issuers (including SEs making ZCZP issues) and intermediaries alike. Cross-Exam Context: III-A / III-C (Compliance) drill deeper into PFUTP; XXIII tests its application to SSE listings where a misleading AIR or baseline could constitute fraud on retail donors/investors. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Never sign an AIR with 'reckless' language — e.g., 'approximately 50,000 beneficiaries served' without sampling evidence. Even if you do not gain anything, a reckless statement inducing investor action can be actionable under PFUTP. Use only URN-backed, sampled, and reconciled figures.
